name: Half-Bridge-SSHI
rationale: The previous Parallel-SSHI-Bridge used a full-bridge rectifier, which incurs two diode drops. Given the low open-circuit voltage (~3.2V), these drops are significant and likely caused the output to settle below 1.8V on several conditions (S1, S2, S4). By using a half-bridge rectifier (tying pzn to ground) combined with a synchronous flip at both voltage extrema (SSHI), we reduce the diode drop to a single DSCH diode. This increase in efficiency, paired with a smaller storage capacitor to improve startup time and settlement (avoiding the long time constants seen in the reference FBR), should allow the circuit to meet the vout_min and startup requirements across all scenarios while the Zener clamp handles the strong excitation of S3.
